goals: Mechanistic: characterize the seasonal ET cycle and its spatial variation across the Passaic basin, attributing contrasts to land cover and soil
Validation: compare simulated seasonal ET to local eddy-covariance flux towers

model_choice.rationale: Single-column ELM simulates full ET partitioning and its seasonal cycle at each point; spatial sampling across the basin's land-cover/soil heterogeneity characterizes ET variation.

answerable: Seasonal ET climatology and its cycle at each column from NLDAS 1980-2018 forcing
Soil-texture control on ET (SSURGO is a first-class per-column lever)
Spatial ET contrast across the basin under native surface conditions

not_answerable.aspect: Validation of seasonal ET against local eddy-covariance flux towers
not_answerable.why: Brief states EC flux towers are absent from the data stack; the framework can only validate where observations exist and cannot fabricate co-located ET data
not_answerable.needs: eddy-covariance / FLUXNET ET observation ingest for the domain (or an accepted analog tower)

not_answerable.aspect: Clean attribution of ET contrast to land cover (urban vs forest vs wetland)
not_answerable.why: Per-column vegetation/PFT differs only via surface-dataset (fsurdat) edits, which are not among the guaranteed run levers; without it land-cover effects are confounded with native soil/forcing

not_answerable.aspect: Indirect ET validation via basin water balance (ET as residual of P - Q - dS) using USGS gauges
not_answerable.why: Single columns have no lateral routing; integrated streamflow for gage comparison needs an explicit aggregation/routing step
not_answerable.needs: runoff routing / multi-column aggregation to gauge

sampling_strategy.n_justification: 3 functionally distinct land-cover regimes x 2 dominant soil textures = 6 core cells, with 2x light replication across the elevation/precip gradient to separate soil-driven ET spread from noise. Smallest set that resolves the ET-driver contrast the question asks for.
sampling_strategy.placement_logic: Concentrate in the urbanized lower Passaic (low ET, high runoff), the forested northern highlands (transpiration-dominated ET, higher precip), and riparian/wetland bottoms (energy- vs water-limited transition), which span the basin's ET regimes.
sampling_strategy.replication: One duplicate per land-cover regime placed at a different elevation/precip band to test forcing sensitivity of the seasonal ET cycle.

sampling_plan.reason: Low-ET, high-imperviousness regime of the lower basin; isolates developed land cover on reduced transpiration and altered seasonal ET.
Same land cover, contrasting soil texture; separates soil-drainage control on evaporation within the urban zone.
Transpiration-dominated forest ET on well-drained soil; captures the phenology-driven summer ET peak.
Forest ET where finer soil sustains moisture later in the season; tests water- vs energy-limited seasonal ET.
Shallow-water-table valley bottoms with highest evaporative demand met; marks the energy-limited end of the ET spectrum.
Duplicates at higher-elevation NLDAS cells to gauge orographic precip sensitivity of the seasonal ET cycle.

validation_design.comparison: analog — no in-domain EC tower exists; at best compare against a similar-land-cover FLUXNET/Ameriflux site outside the basin, clearly labelled analog process validation, NOT co-located
validation_design.metric: seasonal-cycle correlation + bias in monthly ET

validation_design.comparison: co-located at wells near columns — constrains root-zone moisture supply underpinning ET, not ET itself

validation_design.target_variable: streamflow / basin water balance (indirect ET check)
validation_design.comparison: aggregated — ET inferred as P - Q - dS residual; requires multi-column routing/aggregation not yet built

experiment_summary.primary_treatment: baseline NLDAS forcing, native land cover, SSURGO soil, with short spin-up / WTD-informed warm start for seasonal soil-moisture realism

requires_capabilities.why: user's stated validation target; no EC tower in the data stack for this basin
requires_capabilities.blocks: co-located seasonal ET validation (the primary validation goal)

requires_capabilities.why: land cover is the dominant ET driver but is not a guaranteed run lever
requires_capabilities.blocks: clean attribution of ET contrast to land cover

requires_capabilities.capability: runoff routing / multi-column aggregation to USGS gauge
requires_capabilities.why: single columns have no lateral transport, so integrated streamflow is unavailable
requires_capabilities.blocks: indirect water-balance validation of ET via gauges

requires_capabilities.why: seasonal root-zone moisture cycle governs ET and cold-start states are artifacts

assumptions: Native land cover per column is used unless the surface-dataset lever is available; land-cover strata are then approximate proxies via location.
NLDAS-2 covers the CONUS Passaic domain at 0.125 degrees.
SSURGO soil texture is available for per-column assignment.
USGS wells/gauges exist near the sampled zones but their density is unknown.
open_questions: Is any analog Ameriflux/FLUXNET tower (e.g. northeastern deciduous forest or urban site) acceptable as a labelled analog for ET validation?
Can a surface-dataset (PFT) lever be enabled so land cover can be varied explicitly rather than only via native location?
Is a routing/aggregation step planned so USGS gauges can provide an indirect ET water-balance check?
What are the well/gauge locations and densities in-domain?
